statements.claim: The suta Romaharshana was cut down by a blade of kusha grass in the enclosure at Naimisha where he had been reciting, and the sages raised the cry of brahma-hatya.
statements.evidence: Corpus-chain previous title (DKS_0358): 'seeing the suta Romaharshana seated without rising to honor the sages, kills him with a blade of kusha grass; the sages cry out that he has committed brahma-hatya.'

statements.claim: Balarama had come to the Naimisha forest as a pilgrim while the sages were gathered for their great sacrifice.
statements.evidence: Pack index/canonical event evt_0273 (SB 10.78.32-39) sets the scene at Naimisha; prior-story chain frames the pilgrimage and the ongoing recitation.

statements.claim: Romaharshana remained seated, failing to rise to honor the sages.
statements.evidence: Corpus-chain previous title states he was seated without rising to honor the sages.

statements.claim: As the first part of atonement the sages told Balarama to slay the demon Balvala, son of Ilvala, who at every parvan came down from the sky and rained filth upon the sacrifice.
statements.evidence: Excerpt: 'his atonement is to slay the cruel demon Balvala, son of Ilvala, who rains filth upon their sacrifice at every parvan.'

statements.claim: Year after year Balvala broke their rites and they were powerless; the defiled sacrifice had to be begun again from the first offering.
statements.evidence: Repeated defilement at every parvan is supported ('defiling what years of penance had made pure'); the restart-from-the-first-offering detail is dramatized consequence of the defilement, not contradicted by the pack.

statements.claim: The second part of the penance was twelve months of wandering through Bharatavarsha, bathing at the sacred fords to be purified.
statements.evidence: Excerpt: 'then to wander Bharatavarsha bathing at the sacred fords for twelve months to be purified.'

statements.claim: Balarama accepted both tasks without defense or argument, undertaking the expiation for the benefit of the world.
statements.evidence: Excerpt: 'Balarama accepts, undertaking the expiation for the world's benefit.'

statements.claim: The penance would begin at the next parvan when Balvala came again to rain filth on the fire.
statements.evidence: Next-title chain (DKS_0360): 'When Balvala appears at the sacrifice raining impurity, Balarama drags him down'; consistent with the excerpt.

notes: Matches the pack's rendering of SB 10.78.32-39; the killing background is drawn from the pack's own corpus chain.

statements.claim: At the next parvan the demon Balvala appeared over the sacrificial hall, raining filth and impurity onto the fire and offerings.
statements.evidence: SB 10.79.1: 'tato 'medhya-mayaM varSaM balvalena vinirmitam' (a rain of impure matter made by Balvala); excerpt.

statements.claim: Balvala, son of Ilvala, was a sky-roamer who had descended at every parvan to defile the sacrifice.
statements.evidence: Excerpt and prior-story canon (DKS_0359); verse 4 'gagane-caram' (moving in the sky).

statements.claim: Balarama saw the demon huge and black, like a mountain of crushed collyrium.
statements.evidence: 10.79.2: 'bRhat-kAyaM bhinnA~njana-cayopamam' (huge body like a mass of crushed collyrium).

statements.claim: Balarama remembered his plough and mace, the weapons that had torn apart enemy armies.
statements.evidence: 10.79.3: 'sasmAra mUSalaM rAmaH para-sainya-vidAraNam'; excerpt mentions plough and mace.

statements.claim: He caught the sky-roaming Balvala with the tip of his plough and dragged him down; the demon fell to the earth with his forehead split and blood streaming.
statements.evidence: 10.79.4-5: 'tam AkRSya halAgreNa balvalaM gagane-caram / so 'patad bhuvi nirbhinna-lalATo 'sRk samutsRjan.'

statements.claim: Balarama crushed the demon's skull with his mace, and the rain of impurity stopped.
statements.evidence: Excerpt: 'crushes his skull with the mace'; cessation follows the demon's death in the narrative flow of verses 1-8.

statements.claim: The delighted sages praised Balarama with unfailing blessings and gave him the vaijayanti garland of unfading lotuses and garments from heaven.
statements.evidence: 10.79.6-7: 'saMstutya munayo rAmaM prayujyAvitathASiSaH / vaijayantIM dadur mAlAM SrI-dhAmAmlAna-pa~NkajAm'; excerpt adds 'garments.'

statements.claim: With the sages' leave Balarama set out with the brahmanas toward the river Kaushiki — the first steps of his twelve-month pilgrimage.
statements.evidence: 10.79.8: 'atha tair abhyanuj~nAtaH kausikIm etya brAhmaNaiH' (then, permitted by them, he went to the Kaushiki with the brahmanas); pilgrimage per DKS_0359 canon.

notes: Closely follows SB 10.79.1-8 including verse-specific details (collyrium body, split forehead, plough-tip drag).

statements.claim: The rain that lashed Vrindavan for seven nights had ceased; Govardhana had been lifted, held and set down by Krishna, and the cattle were safe.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.74 vv.13-17: kine saved, Govardhana held up, 'this excessive rain extending over seven nights.'

statements.claim: Indra descended on his elephant Airavata, rut-juice trickling, resembling a rainless cloud, to see Krishna.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha v.2: 'seated on his elephant Airavata with temporal juice trickling down and resembling a cloud without water he came down on earth.'

statements.claim: Indra's wonder overcame his anger as he watched the mountain raised, and he desired to see Krishna.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha v.1: 'filled with great surprise and felt a desire for seeing Krishna.'

statements.claim: Indra found Krishna seated at ease at the foot of Govardhana, playing in the forest, engaged in human actions, in a milkman's guise, with the Srivatsa mark and dark-blue-lotus hue, a sun-bright crown, celestial earrings and a jewel necklace, while Garuda, invisible to mortals, shaded him with his wings.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha vv.3-11 (Srivatsa mark, dark-blue lotus hue, sun-effulgent crown, celestial ear-rings, necklace of Padmakanta jewels, playing in the forest engaged in human actions) and Vishnu Purana 5.12 ('Garuda, the king of birds, invisible to mortals, spreading out his wings to shade the head of Hari').

statements.claim: Indra acknowledged that he had sent the seven-night deluge in anger at his worship being set aside, and that Krishna had put down the rain by his own power in Indra's very presence.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha vv.16-17: 'I sent down this excessive rain extending over seven nights and destructive of the kine which even the Devas and Danavas cannot withstand. But thou hast, by thy own power, put down this terrible shower in my very presence.'

statements.claim: Indra praised Krishna: as gold is foremost among metals so Krishna is foremost of the celestials; he alone is eternal among the gods, and Indra sees no second who could carry the mountain.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha vv.21-25: 'Thou art alone eternal amongst the gods... I do not see a second capable of carrying the weight thou hast held'; 'As gold is among the metals...'; 'so thou art the foremost of the celestials.'

statements.claim: Indra said a portion of himself had been born on earth as Arjuna, son of Pritha — Krishna's cousin — who in the coming war of the Bharatas would be Krishna's friend and help in battle; he asked Krishna to befriend him, instruct him in spiritual knowledge and care for him as for Indra himself.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.12: 'A portion of me has been born as Arjuna, the son of Pritha'; Harivamsha excerpt: 'he will be thy friend and help in battle... do thou instruct him in spiritual knowledge... always regard and take care of him as thou dost me'; index summary: 'Indra asks Krishna to protect his son Arjuna, Krishna's cousin, in the coming war of the Bharatas.'

statements.claim: Krishna answered that he knew Arjuna and would befriend him as long as he continued upon the earth.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.12: 'I know thy son... and I will befriend him as long as I continue upon earth.'

statements.claim: Indra returned to heaven and the friendship of the two future warriors was sealed unseen by the cowherds.
statements.evidence: Closing frame consistent with both sources; the pack records no contrary detail.

notes: Follows the Harivamsha version per the tradition_note, with the Arjuna request corroborated by both Harivamsha 1.74 and Vishnu Purana 5.12 excerpts.

statements.claim: The bow of the svayamvara had beaten every king: Rukma, Sunitha, Vakra, Karna (son of Radha), Duryodhana and Salya all failed to string it.
statements.evidence: MB 1.190 (Ganguli): 'that bow which Rukma, Sunitha, Vakra, Radha's son, Duryodhana, Salya, and many other kings... could not even with great exertion, string.'

statements.claim: Draupadi, daughter of Drupada, was to be won by whoever could string the bow and shoot the mark through the hole in the wheel.
statements.evidence: Index summary; MB 1.190: mark 'shot... through the hole in the machine above which it had been placed.'

statements.claim: The brahmanas debated: some feared a stripling would mock the whole body of brahmanas; others cited Rama son of Jamadagni defeating all the Kshatriyas and Agastya drinking the ocean, saying brahmanas are strong in their own energy and must never be despised.
statements.evidence: MB 1.190: 'Rama the son of Jamadagni defeated in battle, all the Kshatriyas. Agastya by his Brahma energy drank off the fathomless ocean... Brahmanas are ever strong in their own energy. One should never disregard a Brahmana.'

statements.claim: The youth was Arjuna (Jishnu), the middle Pandava, of the complexion of Indra's banner, disguised as a brahmana.
statements.evidence: MB 1.190: 'the high-souled Jishnu arose from among the crowd of Brahmanas seated in that assembly... possessing the complexion of Indra's banner.'

statements.claim: Arjuna walked around the bow, bowed to Ishana the giver of boons, remembered Krishna, and strung the bow in the twinkling of an eye.
statements.evidence: MB 1.190: 'walking round that bow, and bending his head unto that giver of boons--the lord Isana--and remembering Krishna also, he took it up... strung in the twinkling of an eye.'

statements.claim: Taking the five arrows, he shot the mark, which fell to the ground through the hole.
statements.evidence: MB 1.190: 'taking up the five arrows he shot the mark and caused it to fall down on the ground through the hole in the machine.'

statements.claim: The gods showered celestial flowers on the slayer of foes; thousands of brahmanas waved their upper garments; musicians and bards celebrated; the failed kings cried out in grief.
statements.evidence: MB 1.190 passage ('the gods showered celestial flowers on the head of Partha the slayer of foes... thousands of Brahmanas began to wave their upper garments in joy... the monarchs who had been unsuccessful, uttered exclamations of grief and despair').

statements.claim: Drupada was filled with joy and ready to aid the victor with his forces, while Yudhishthira and the twins slipped quietly away to their lodging.
statements.evidence: MB 1.190: 'the monarch desired to assist with his forces the hero if the occasion arose... Yudhishthira... accompanied by... the twins, hastily left the amphitheatre for returning to his temporary home.'

statements.claim: Krishna, filled with joy, approached the son of Kunti with a white robe and a garland of flowers and placed them on him.
statements.evidence: MB 1.190 excerpt: 'And Krishna beholding the mark shot and beholding Partha also like unto Indra himself... was filled with joy, and approached the son of Kunti with a white robe and a garland of flowers.'

statements.claim: Arjuna was saluted with reverence by all the brahmanas and left the lists followed closely by Draupadi, who had become his wife.
statements.evidence: MB 1.190: 'was saluted with reverence by all the Brahmanas. And he soon after left the lists followed close by her who thus became his wife.'

notes: Nearly a verbatim retelling of the Ganguli 1.190 passage supplied in the pack.

statements.claim: Krishna saw the five disguised Pandavas among the Brahmins and perceived them as mighty elephants drawn toward a lotus-covered lake, or fire covered by ashes.
statements.evidence: MB 1.189 excerpt: 'beholding those elephants in rut--the five (Pandavas)--attracted towards Draupadi like mighty elephants towards a lake overgrown with lotuses, or like fire covered with ashes, Krishna... began.'

statements.claim: One after another the kings failed to string the great bow, tossed to the ground, panting, with crowns loosened and garlands disordered.
statements.evidence: MB 1.189: 'were tossed on the ground and lay perfectly motionless for some time. Their strength spent and their crowns and garlands loosened from their persons, they began to pant for breath.'

statements.claim: Karna strung the bow easily, but Draupadi refused a Suta ('I will not select a Suta for my lord'), and Karna threw the drawn bow aside, laughing in vexation.
statements.evidence: MB 1.189: 'quickly raising it strung it and placed the arrows on the string... But seeing Karna, Draupadi loudly said, I will not select a Suta for my lord. Then Karna, laughing in vexation... threw aside the bow already drawn to a circle.'

statements.claim: A Brahmana seated among the priests rose, strung the stiff bow as if it were a reed and pierced the golden mark, and Krishna, filled with joy, greeted him with a white robe and a garland.
statements.evidence: MB 1.190 (in chain with this story) records the Brahmana's feat and Krishna's joyful greeting with white robe and garland; DKS_0362 evidence supplies the stringing detail. 'As if it were a reed' is mild embellishment of the feat.

statements.claim: The furious kings resolved to slay Drupada for giving his daughter to a Brahmana; Drupada, pale with fear, sought the Brahmanas' protection; Bhima tore up a tree like an elephant and stood near Arjuna like Yama with his mace, while Arjuna stood ready with his bow.
statements.evidence: MB 1.191: kings' speech ('Passing us by and treating the assembled monarchs as straw... let us slay him'); Drupada 'sought, from fear, the protection of the Brahmanas'; 'the mighty Bhima... tore up like an elephant a large tree and divested it of its leaves... stood, like unto the mace-bearing king of the dead (Yama)... near Arjuna'; Arjuna 'shaking off all fear he stood with his bow ready.'

statements.claim: Krishna named the five brothers to Balarama: Arjuna by his lion-tread and four-cubit bow, Bhima (Vrikodara) by the tree feat, Yudhishthira by his lotus eyes and four-cubit height, and the twins as sons of the twin Aswins, having heard they escaped the house of lac with Pritha.
statements.evidence: MB 1.191 speech matches nearly verbatim: bow 'four full cubits in length, is Arjuna! There is no doubt... if I am Vasudeva'; Vrikodara and the tree feat; Yudhishthira 'of eyes like unto lotus-petals, of full four cubits height... is Dharma's son'; 'the two other youths, like unto Kartikeya, are, I suspect, the sons of the twin Aswins'; 'the sons of Pandu along with their mother Pritha had all escaped from the conflagration of the house of lac.'

statements.claim: Krishna had recognized them earlier, murmuring to Balarama 'That is Yudhishthira; that is Bhima with Jishnu; and those are the twin heroes,' and Balarama cast a glance of quiet satisfaction.
statements.evidence: MB 1.189: 'he said unto Rama (Valadeva), That is Yudhishthira; that is Bhima with Jishnu (Arjuna); and those are the twin heroes. And Rama surveying them slowly cast a glance of satisfaction at Krishna.'

statements.claim: Balarama rejoiced that their father's sister Pritha and the foremost Kaurava princes had escaped death.
statements.evidence: MB 1.191: 'O, I am happy to hear, as I do from sheer good fortune, that our father's sister Pritha with the foremost of the Kaurava princes have all escaped (from death)!'

statements.claim: The monarchs, biting their nether lips in wrath, saw only the two Brahmins in the fray and did not see five princes of the Kuru line.
statements.evidence: MB 1.189: 'Biting their nether lips in wrath, the other heroes there... looked with expanded eyes on Draupadi alone without noticing the Pandavas.'

statements.claim: Krishna kept the secret, saying nothing publicly.
statements.evidence: Consistent with the sources, which record Krishna naming the brothers privately to Balarama only; no public announcement appears in the pack.

notes: Identification speeches track the Ganguli 1.189/1.191 passages closely; the story merges the early 1.189 recognition with the later 1.191 naming, as the pack itself notes both chapters record the scene.

statements.claim: The kings rose in fury against Drupada for bestowing his daughter on a Brahmana, crying that the svayamvara is for Kshatriyas and rushing to slay him and his son; Drupada, pale with fear, sought the Brahmanas' protection.
statements.evidence: MB 1.191 (in chain) and 1.192: 'Passing us by and treating the assembled monarchs as straw... this Drupada desires to bestow his daughter on a Brahmana'; 'The Vedic declaration is well-known that the Swayamvara is for the Kshatriyas. The Brahmanas have no claim...'; 'let us slay him... along with his son'; 'sought, from fear, the protection of the Brahmanas.'

statements.claim: The Brahmins shook their deer-skins and cocoanut-shell water-pots, crying 'Fear not, we will fight the foe'; Arjuna, smiling, asked them to stand aside as spectators, saying he would check the monarchs with showers of arrows like snakes checked by mantras.
statements.evidence: MB 1.192: 'those bulls among Brahmanas shaking their deer-skins and water-pots made of cocoanut-shells exclaimed, Fear not, we will fight the foe! Arjuna smilingly... said, Stand ye aside as spectators (of the fray) Showering hundreds of arrows furnished with straight points even I shall check, like snakes with mantras, all those angry monarchs.'

statements.claim: Taking up the great bow he had won, Arjuna stood immovable as a mountain with Bhima at his side.
statements.evidence: MB 1.192: 'the mighty Arjuna taking up the bow he had obtained as dower accompanied by his brother Bhima stood immovable as a mountain.'

statements.claim: Karna rushed at Jishnu, and Salya, king of Madra, charged Bhima like an elephant for a she-elephant in heat.
statements.evidence: MB 1.192: 'Karna endued with great energy rushed against Jishnu for fight. And Salya the mighty king of Madra rushed against Bhima like an elephant rushing against another for the sake of a she-elephant in heat.'

statements.claim: Arjuna pierced Karna with sharp arrows until he fainted; Karna recovered and fought with greater care, and the two became invisible to the spectators, enveloped in each other's arrow-showers, exchanging words intelligible only to heroes.
statements.evidence: MB 1.192: 'drew his tough bow and pieced him with his sharp arrows... made Radheya (Karna) faint. Recovering consciousness Karna attacked Arjuna with greater care... (each enveloped by the other's shower of arrows) they both became invisible... Behold the strength of my arms.--Mark, how I have counteracted that feat,--those were the words--intelligible to heroes alone.'

statements.claim: Karna asked whether Arjuna was the science of weapons embodied, Rama, Indra, or Vishnu in a Brahmana's form; Arjuna answered that he was only a Brahmana, foremost of warriors, accomplished in the Brahma and Paurandara weapons, and bade him wait; Karna desisted, deeming Brahma energy invincible.
statements.evidence: MB 1.192 dialogue, ending: 'Karna the adopted son of Radha desisted from the fight, for that mighty chariot-fighter thought that Brahma energy is ever invincible.'

statements.claim: Salya and Bhima fought like two elephants in rut with clenched fists and knees, the lists ringing like the clash of granite masses, until Bhima hurled Salya down gently, without hurting him much.
statements.evidence: MB 1.192: 'struck each other with their clenched fists and knees... blows hard as the clash of two masses of granite... taking up Salya on his arms hurled him to a distance... though he threw Salya on the ground he did it without hurting him much.'

statements.claim: The alarmed monarchs murmured that only Rama, Drona or Kiriti son of Pandu could face Karna, and only Krishna could face Duryodhana.
statements.evidence: MB 1.192: 'Who can encounter Karna, the son of Radha, in fight, except Rama or Drona, or Kiriti, the son of Pandu? Who also can encounter Duryodhana in battle except Krishna...'

statements.claim: Krishna, having beheld Bhima's feat and believing the two were sons of Kunti, gently told the monarchs 'This maiden hath been justly acquired,' and they desisted from the fight.
statements.evidence: MB 1.192 excerpt: 'And Krishna, having beheld that feat of Bhima, believed them both to be the son of Kunti. And gently addressing the assembled monarchs, saying, This maiden hath been justly acquired (by the Brahmana), he induced them to abandon the fight. Accomplished in battle, those monarchs then desisted from the fight.'

notes: Long quoted passages track the Ganguli 1.192 text nearly verbatim.

statements.claim: The brothers returned to the potter's house and told their mother they had brought alms; Kunti, not having seen them, answered from within 'Enjoy ye all what ye have obtained,' then saw Draupadi and cried 'Oh, what have I said?'
statements.evidence: MB 1.193: 'represented Yajnaseni unto their mother as the alms they had obtained that day. And Kunti who was there within the room and saw not her sons, replied, saying, Enjoy ye all (what ye have obtained). The moment after, she beheld Krishna [Draupadi] and then she said, Oh, what have I said?'

statements.claim: Anxious from fear of sin, Kunti asked Yudhishthira how her speech might not become untrue, how sin might not touch the daughter of the king of Panchala, and how she might not become uneasy.
statements.evidence: MB 1.193: 'tell me how my speech may not become untrue; how sin may not touch the daughter of the king of Panchala, and how also she may not become uneasy.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira consoled his mother and told Arjuna, who had won Yajnasena's daughter, to wed her with due rites before the sacred fire.
statements.evidence: MB 1.193: 'reflecting for a moment, consoled Kunti, and addressing Dhananjaya, said, By thee, O Phalguna, hath Yajnaseni been won... igniting the sacred fire, take thou her hand with due rites.'

statements.claim: Arjuna refused, urging that Yudhishthira wed first, then Bhima, then himself, then Nakula and last Sahadeva, and that all were obedient to the king.
statements.evidence: MB 1.193: 'Thou shouldst wed first, then the strong-armed Bhima of inconceivable feats, then myself, then Nakula, and last of all, Sahadeva... All of us are obedient to thee. O, command us as thou likest.'

statements.claim: The beauty of Panchali, fashioned by the Creator, stirred the god of desire in the brothers; Yudhishthira remembered the words of the sage Krishna-Dwaipayana and, fearing division among the brothers, declared 'The auspicious Draupadi shall be the common wife of us all.'
statements.evidence: MB 1.193: 'the lavishing beauty of Panchali who had been modelled by the Creator himself... the God of Desire invaded their hearts and continued to crush all their senses... Yudhishthira... recollected the words of Krishna-Dwaipayana. And the king, then, from fear of a division amongst the brothers... said, The auspicious Draupadi shall be the common wife of us all.'

statements.claim: Krishna, suspecting the svayamvara Brahmanas were the Pandavas, came with Balarama to the potter's house; they touched Yudhishthira's feet (Krishna saying 'I am Krishna'), rejoiced with the Pandavas, and also touched the feet of Kunti, their father's sister.
statements.evidence: MB 1.193: 'Krishna suspecting the five persons he had seen at the Swayamvara to be none else than the heroes of the Kuru race, came accompanied by the son of Rohini (Valadeva), to the house of the potter... Then Vasudeva approaching that foremost of virtuous men--the son of Kunti--and touching the feet of that prince... said, I am Krishna. And the son of Rohini (Valadeva) also approaching Yudhishthira, did the same... those heroes of the Yadu race thereafter touched also the feet of Kunti, their father's sister.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira asked Krishna how he had traced them while they lived in disguise.
statements.evidence: MB 1.193: 'Ajatasatru... asked, How, O Vasudeva, hast thou been able to trace us, as we are living in disguise?'

statements.claim: Krishna answered that fire, even covered, can be known; no one but the Pandavas could show such might; by sheer good fortune they escaped the fierce fire and the wicked son of Dhritarashtra did not succeed; they should grow like a fire in a cave, and he and Balarama should return lest any monarch recognize them.
statements.evidence: MB 1.193: 'fire, even if it is covered, can be known. Who else among men than the Pandavas could exhibit such might?... by sheer good fortune have ye escaped from that fierce fire... the wicked son of Dhritarashtra and his counsellors have not succeeded... grow ye in prosperity like a fire in a cave... And lest any of the monarchs recognise ye, let us return.'

statements.claim: The two Yadava princes left as quietly as they had come, leaving the potter's house to keep its secret.
statements.evidence: Closing frame consistent with Krishna's 'let us return'; no contrary detail in the pack.

notes: Faithful to the Ganguli 1.193 passage; the story renders Draupadi where the translation names her Krishnaa/Yajnaseni.

statements.claim: After the alliance with the Pandavas, Drupada's fears were dispelled and he no longer stood in fear even of the gods.
statements.evidence: MB 1.201: 'King Drupada, after his alliance with the Pandavas, had all his fears dispelled. Indeed, the monarch no longer stood in fear even of the gods.'

statements.claim: The ladies of Drupada's household worshipped Kunti's feet, naming themselves one by one; Draupadi, in red silk with the auspicious thread at her wrists, saluted her mother-in-law and stood before her with joined palms.
statements.evidence: MB 1.201: 'The ladies of the illustrious Drupada's household approached Kunti and introduced themselves unto her, mentioning their respective names, and worshipped her feet... Krishna also, attired in red silk and her wrists still encircled with the auspicious thread, saluting her mother-in-law with reverence, stood contentedly before her with joined palms.'

statements.claim: Kunti blessed Draupadi, wishing her to be as Sachi to Indra, Swaha to Vibhavasu, Rohini to Soma, Damayanti to Nala, Arundhati to Vasishtha and Lakshmi to Narayana; the mother of long-lived heroic children; installed as queen of Kurujangala with Yudhishthira; and to rejoice again at seeing her the mother of a son, as she rejoiced at the red silk.
statements.evidence: MB 1.201 blessing (all six similes quoted in the text; the story abridges by omitting 'Bhadra unto Vaisravana' and other clauses — abridgement, not contradiction); 'Be thou the mother of long-lived and heroic children... Be thou installed as the Queen of the kingdom and the capital of Kurujangala, with thy husband Yudhishthira the just... as I rejoice today beholding thee attired in red silk, so shall I rejoice again, when... I behold thee become the mother of a son.'

statements.claim: After the sons of Pandu were married, Krishna sent them gold ornaments set with pearls and black gems (lapis lazuli), costly robes from various countries, soft blankets, valuable hides, beds, carpets, vehicles, vessels by the hundreds set with gems and diamonds, female servants by the thousands, trained elephants from Madra, horses in costly harness and chariots drawn by fine horses.
statements.evidence: MB 1.201 catalogue matches item for item, including 'well-trained elephants brought from the country of Madra, and many excellent horses in costly harness, cars drawn by horses of excellent colours and large teeth.'

statements.claim: The slayer of Madhu also sent coins of pure gold by crores upon crores, laid out in separate heaps.
statements.evidence: MB 1.201: 'The slayer of Madhu, of immeasurable soul, also sent them coins of pure gold by crores upon crores in separate heaps.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira the just, desirous of gratifying Govinda, accepted all the presents with great joy.
statements.evidence: MB 1.201: 'And Yudhishthira the just, desirous of gratifying Govinda, accepted all those presents with great joy.'

statements.claim: The interpretive close — gifts as an alliance declared openly by a cousin who recognized the brothers in a crowd and never said their names aloud; not payment or dowry but a welcome and a promise that the hidden princes would not stay hidden long.
statements.evidence: Thematic framing consistent with the source (which records no accompanying message); not asserted as a sourceable fact.

notes: Gift catalogue and blessing follow MB 1.201 (Ganguli) nearly verbatim; Drupada's relief cites the passage directly.
